findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image? is extension-only, so any logged-in user can rename an arbitrary file (or a PNG decompression bomb) to .png and have ImageMagick decode it synchronously in the web process with no resource limits or rate limiting.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Each pass runs convert plus the full ImageOptim chain on a multi-MB image, up to 5 times per request, with no rate limit; a user can spam 10MB uploads that can never get under the limit to burn web-worker CPU.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ImageOptim (run inside convert_with) replaces the file via rename, detaching the open Tempfile fd from tempfile.path; after pass 1 tempfile.size is stale so the loop cannot observe progress, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize and stores bytes read from the old inode while sha1 is computed from the new path.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored; when convert fails (non-image, corrupt file, unsupported geometry) the identical failing command is re-run 4 more times before the upload is rejected anyway.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails off (the default) downsize_instructions uses `from[0]`, so a large animated GIF has its original upload silently flattened to the first frame, not just its thumbnails.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails on, GIFs go to gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which does not accept percentage geometry (only WxH / --scale), so large animated GIFs are never downsized and still fail as too large.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — convert writes its output in place over the input path; if it is OOM-killed or crashes mid-write (likely with a bomb) the tempfile is left truncated/corrupt and, now being small enough, is stored as the user's upload.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Raising the download cap to 10.megabytes means FileHelper.download's truncated partial file for a >10MB remote image is no longer rejected by size validation but downsized under the limit and stored corrupt; the `rescue nil` also still hides the download failure and yields a nil tempfile with no error.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Ruby has no overloading: this `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently replaces the `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` defined at line 145, so the first is dead code and any existing 5-argument caller (e.g. profile/card background resizing in Upload.create_for) now raises ArgumentError.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — A JPEG renamed to .png is re-encoded as PNG by ImageMagick (output format follows the tempfile extension), which can grow the file rather than shrink it, while the client-supplied content_type is still trusted downstream.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — tempfile.path embeds the user-controlled extension (Rack preserves File.extname of the original filename, after percent-unescaping) and is interpolated unquoted into a backtick shell command; `foo.png%0A` passes the `\.png$` check and injects a newline into the command line.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client now hardcodes a 10MB limit for every upload type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb and any admin-raised max_image_size_kb, so attachments are fully uploaded before the server rejects them and the 413/too-large messages quote a limit the server does not enforce.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the 5-arg `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` defined at line 145, so the 5-arg version is dead code and any existing caller passing width and height separately (e.g. Upload.create_for's downsize path) now raises ArgumentError or misparses opts.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Passing "80%" as dimensions with `allow_animation:` set routes animated GIFs to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which gifsicle rejects (needs WxH; percentages use --scale), so convert_with returns false and the 5-iteration loop never shrinks oversized animated GIFs, which are then rejected by Upload.create_for.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — self.optimize` public signature changed from (operation, from, to, width, height, opts) to (operation, from, to, dimensions, opts) and public `self.dimensions(width, height)` was removed without a deprecation shim, breaking any external/plugin callers of these class methods.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — validateUploadedFiles` now hardcodes a 10MB client limit for every upload `type`, ignoring `max_<type>_size_kb` (including `max_attachment_size_kb`), so attachments over the admin-configured limit pass client validation and fail server-side with a less helpful error, while sites configured above 10MB are wrongly blocked.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now reports a hardcoded 10240 KB in the `file_too_large` message regardless of the actual server/nginx limit or `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb`, giving users an incorrect limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL-download path replaces the `max_image_size_kb` limit with a fixed 10MB for all types, so attachment URLs are now capped at 10MB regardless of `max_attachment_size_kb` and image URLs larger than 10MB are silently dropped (rescue nil) even if the site allows them.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Auto-downsize loop runs `convert from[0]` in place on the original upload when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is false (or the extension is not .gif), so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened to its first frame before Upload.create_for sees it.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently replaces the 5-arg `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145, so any existing caller passing width and height separately (e.g. Upload.create_for's max_image_width/max_image_height downsize) now raises ArgumentError (5 for 3..4) or treats the height Integer as opts.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored; when convert/gifsicle fails the loop just spins through all 5 attempts on an unchanged (or possibly truncated, since to==from) file and then proceeds to Upload.create_for with the oversized image instead of surfacing an error.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Passing "80%" for an animated GIF (allow_animated_thumbnails on, .gif path) reaches gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which does not accept percentages, so large animated GIFs can never be downsized and always fail the size check afterwards.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop condition and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for use tempfile.size (fstat on the already-open fd) while downsize/ImageOptim rewrite the file by path (ImageOptim replaces via rename to a new inode), so the open Tempfile can point at a stale inode with a stale size/content, making the loop and stored filesize/sha1 inconsistent with what is on disk.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit hard-coded to 10MB for all upload types, but the server still rejects attachments over max_attachment_size_kb (and non-downsizable images over max_image_size_kb), so users now get a late server error and the alert reports a wrong max_size_kb.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — 413 handler now always reports 10MB regardless of the actual web-server body limit, so the message is wrong whenever nginx client_max_body_size differs from 10MB.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image? matches .svg, so an oversized SVG is fed to `convert ... -resize 80%` writing back to a .svg path, which rasterizes/corrupts the vector file rather than shrinking it.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails off, downsize uses `convert from[0]`, so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened to its first frame before being stored as the original upload.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick+ImageOptim shell-outs on a user-supplied file of up to 10MB now run in the upload request/defer thread with no timeout or ImageMagick resource limits (-limit memory/map), so a large or crafted PNG/JPEG can pin a web worker for minutes and exhaust memory; previously oversize files were rejected before any image processing.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — Each downsize pass also runs the full ImageOptim tool chain (jpegoptim/optipng/pngquant etc., often seconds on large images) on an intermediate result that the next loop iteration immediately overwrites; up to 4 of the 5 optimizations are pure wasted CPU.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop ignores the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize, so when convert/gifsicle fails (or the file does not shrink) it re-runs the identical failing command 5 times before Upload.create_for rejects the file anyway.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Tempfile#size on an open Tempfile uses fstat on the original fd, but ImageOptim replaces the file via rename to a new inode, so the observed size never changes and the loop always runs all 5 convert+optimize passes even when the first pass already met the limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — "80%" is per-dimension (~0.64x pixels per pass, ~0.107x after 5), so a 10MB image can only reliably reach ~1MB; with a smaller max_image_size_kb the full 5-pass, up-to-10MB decode/re-encode is done and the upload is still rejected, and there is no early exit when a pass cannot make progress.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:120 — gifsicle --resize-fit does not accept a percentage ("80%"), so the animated-GIF branch (allow_animated_thumbnails) fails every pass, yielding 5 wasted shell-outs and no downsizing for large animated GIFs.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side limit is hardcoded to 10MB for all upload types (including attachments, which are never downsized), so files up to 10MB are fully transferred, written to tempfiles and only then rejected server-side, increasing bandwidth and disk churn relative to the site setting.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL uploads now download up to 10MB from arbitrary remote hosts regardless of max_image_size_kb before any size check, increasing per-request network and disk usage.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, so a failing/absent convert silently loops 5 times and the oversized (or partially written) file is passed on to Upload.create_for with no logging or user-facing error explaining why.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — In-place conversion (from == to on the same tempfile) means an ImageMagick failure after the output is opened (disk full, OOM kill, encoder error) truncates/corrupts the user's original, and because the size then shrinks below the limit the corrupt file is accepted and stored.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert (and ImageOptim) now run synchronously inside the web request via a backtick with no timeout or ImageMagick resource limits, up to 5 times on a 10MB user-controlled image, letting a decompression-bomb PNG/JPEG pin a unicorn worker indefinitely.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — tempfile.size uses fstat on the already-open fd; ImageOptim#optimize_image! replaces the path via rename to a new inode, so after the first pass tempfile.size (loop condition and the filesize passed to Upload.create_for) reports the stale pre-optimization inode and any later fd-based read stores stale content.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, "80%" is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit which requires WxH and rejects percentages, so every oversized animated GIF fails all 5 attempts and is rejected; with it disabled, convert from[0] silently flattens the animated GIF to a single frame in place.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts) silently overrides the (max_width, max_height) overload defined at line 145; any caller using the old 4/5-arg signature now gets ArgumentError or a TypeError from Integer#[] in optimize.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client limit is hard-coded to 10MB for every upload type, so attachments over max_attachment_size_kb (and images on sites with max_image_size_kb above 10MB, or images that still exceed the limit after 5 passes) are uploaded fully then rejected server-side with a different limit than the one the client displayed.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now reports a hard-coded 10MB regardless of the web server's actual client_max_body_size, so users get a misleading limit when the proxy rejects the request.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads are capped at a fixed 10MB independent of max_image_size_kb, and the rescue nil still leaves tempfile nil so tempfile.size at line 72 raises NoMethodError (500) instead of a clean error when the download fails or exceeds the cap.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Any logged-in user can now get ImageMagick `convert` run up to 5 times on unvalidated, arbitrary file content in the web worker (Scheduler::Defer) merely by naming the file *.png/*.jpg, with no -limit/policy or timeout, enabling decompression-bomb DoS and exposing IM coder vulnerabilities before any size/format validation occurs.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Downsize loop runs inside the request/Defer path rather than a background job and each iteration also invokes ImageOptim, so a single oversized upload can tie up the unicorn worker for minutes (CPU/memory exhaustion by ordinary users).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download cap is hardcoded to 10MB instead of the admin-configured max_image_size_kb, so admins can no longer lower the server-side fetch bound for remote URLs.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client-side size check ignores SiteSetting max_*_size_kb (hardcoded 10MB) for all upload types including attachments; server validation still applies, but the UI now reports a false limit and permits sending oversized attachments.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Redefining `self.downsize` with a 3-positional-arg signature silently replaces the 5-arg version at line 145, so any existing spec or caller using `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height[, opts])` now raises ArgumentError/TypeError and no test was updated to cover either signature.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — self.dimensions` was removed and `optimize` now takes a preformatted dimensions string, but no spec asserts the new `resize`/`downsize` -> `optimize` contract; specs that stub `OptimizedImage.dimensions` or `expects(:optimize).with(..., width, height, ...)` would now fail or no longer exercise real code.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — validateUploadedFiles` now ignores `max_image_size_kb`/`max_attachment_size_kb` and hardcodes 10MB, which breaks the existing JS "too big" test that sets `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a small value and expects a `file_too_large` alert; the diff contains no test changes.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error branch now reports a hardcoded 10MB rather than `max_image_size_kb`, a user-visible message change with no test asserting the alert text/value.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — New downsize loop has zero controller spec coverage: no test that an image over `max_image_size_kb` is downsized before `Upload.create_for`, nor that a file under the limit is left untouched.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:65 — No test that the loop gives up after 5 attempts and still proceeds to `Upload.create_for` (letting the upload validator reject an image that could not be shrunk enough).
app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — No test that non-image uploads (`FileHelper.is_image?` false) and `max_image_size_kb == 0` skip the downsize loop entirely.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — OptimizedImage.downsize` return value is ignored; no test for the convert-failure path (loop spins 5 times with the file unchanged and the request still continues).

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL download limit changed from `max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` with no spec covering the new limit or the interaction with the downsize loop for URL-sourced uploads.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Animated GIF branch (`allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` routing to `downsize_instructions_animated`) is untested with the new "80%" percentage dimension string.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — FileHelper.is_image? is extension-only, so any logged-in user can rename an arbitrary file (or a PNG decompression bomb) to .png and have ImageMagick decode it synchronously in the web process with no resource limits or rate limiting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous downsizing loop in `create_upload` that is gated only by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (i.e., a check on the filename, not the actual content) and then invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`, which shells out to ImageMagick via `convert_with`. This introduces a new path where user-supplied uploads (or downloaded URLs) can trigger potentially expensive ImageMagick decoding/processing in the web request with no resource limits shown in the diff. While the finding’s claim that `FileHelper.is_image?` is “extension-only” can’t be verified from the diff, the filename-based gating and synchronous ImageMagick execution are directly evidenced here and are a security/DoS risk newly exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Each pass runs convert plus the full ImageOptim chain on a multi-MB image, up to 5 times per request, with no rate limit; a user can spam 10MB uploads that can never get under the limit to burn web-worker CPU.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that can run up to 5 downsizing passes per request: `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes; OptimizedImage.downsize(...); attempt -= 1; end`. Each pass invokes `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which shells out to an external convert command via `convert_with` (backticks). This creates an obvious CPU-amplification path: a user can repeatedly upload near-10MB images (the JS and URL-download caps were changed to `10 * 1024` KB / `10.megabytes`) that may not shrink below the configured limit, forcing up to 5 expensive conversions per upload request with no mitigation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — ImageOptim (run inside convert_with) replaces the file via rename, detaching the open Tempfile fd from tempfile.path; after pass 1 tempfile.size is stale so the loop cannot observe progress, and Upload.create_for receives a stale filesize and stores bytes read from the old inode while sha1 is computed from the new path.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate explains that the file is replaced via rename, causing the open Tempfile fd to be detached and making `tempfile.size` stale. This directly matches the golden issue about the loop relying on `tempfile.size` potentially not updating after modifications, leading to non-terminating/incorrect loop behavior and incorrect file handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored; when convert fails (non-image, corrupt file, unsupported geometry) the identical failing command is re-run 4 more times before the upload is rejected anyway.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but never checks its return value. In optimized_image.rb, `convert_with` returns `false` when the convert command fails, so a failure won’t stop the loop; if the file size remains above `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, the same failing conversion will be retried until `attempt` hits 0. This is a real, diff-grounded robustness/performance issue (missing failure handling/break), though the claim that it will be "rejected anyway" isn’t directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails off (the default) downsize_instructions uses `from[0]`, so a large animated GIF has its original upload silently flattened to the first frame, not just its thumbnails.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes the *original* uploaded image in-place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`) when it exceeds `max_image_size_kb`. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` only uses the `_animated` instruction path when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true and the file is a `.GIF`; otherwise it uses the non-animated `downsize_instructions`. If `downsize_instructions` selects only the first frame (as the finding claims via `from[0]`), then with `allow_animated_thumbnails` off (default) an animated GIF upload would be flattened, causing silent data loss in the uploaded file, not just thumbnails.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails on, GIFs go to gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which does not accept percentage geometry (only WxH / --scale), so large animated GIFs are never downsized and still fail as too large.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — convert writes its output in place over the input path; if it is OOM-killed or crashes mid-write (likely with a bomb) the tempfile is left truncated/corrupt and, now being small enough, is stored as the user's upload.

adjudication.rationale: The new logic in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes images *in place* by calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, i.e., identical input/output paths. `OptimizedImage.optimize` ultimately runs an external convert command via `convert_with` and does not enforce atomic output or preserve the original tempfile; the controller also ignores the return value. If the convert process crashes or is killed mid-write, the tempfile can be left partially written/truncated, and the subsequent `Upload.create_for(..., tempfile.size, ...)` will store whatever remains (potentially now under the size threshold). This failure mode is enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Raising the download cap to 10.megabytes means FileHelper.download's truncated partial file for a >10MB remote image is no longer rejected by size validation but downsized under the limit and stored corrupt; the `rescue nil` also still hides the download failure and yields a nil tempfile with no error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the remote download limit changing from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to `10.megabytes` and adds an image-downsizing loop based on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. However, the finding’s core claim—that `FileHelper.download` produces a truncated partial file that was previously rejected by size validation but will now be downsized and stored corrupt—cannot be verified from this diff: we don’t see `FileHelper.download`’s truncation behavior, any size-validation logic in `Upload.create_for`, or that a truncated file would be accepted and saved. The note about `rescue nil` hiding download errors is true but it already existed in the same line and isn’t newly introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — A JPEG renamed to .png is re-encoded as PNG by ImageMagick (output format follows the tempfile extension), which can grow the file rather than shrink it, while the client-supplied content_type is still trusted downstream.

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side “auto-reduce” loop in `create_upload` runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place, while still passing the original `content_type = file.content_type` to `Upload.create_for(...)`. Because ImageMagick/convert typically determines output encoding from the destination filename, and here the destination is `tempfile.path` (which in common Rails/Rack upload flows is derived from the client-provided filename/extension), a mislabeled upload (e.g., JPEG bytes but `.png` name) can be re-encoded to PNG, potentially increasing size and also leaving `content_type` inconsistent with the rewritten file.
